# Housekeeping: audit

## Authorized scope and smallest closable slice

Review the complete `tools/audit` Cargo package and its tests. Deliver practical, behavior-preserving cleanup in this package, or an evidenced no-change verdict when existing choices earn their cost. Cover all five user requests: repeated code/LoC; load-bearing test purposes; avoidable copies; applicable micro SIMD; and data structures that cap efficiency. The user requests two GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agents concurrently; this overrides the default Terra implementation model for this workflow. Root Sol owns briefing, adversarial review, exact-path checkpoints, integration and remote synchronization.

## Frozen boundaries

Existing public APIs, feature behavior, canonical/wire identities, arithmetic order and per-lane rendered bits, latency/tail, link modes, smoothing and NaN/denormal rules remain contractual. Zero render allocations/frees, locks, I/O or syscalls; no runtime native ISA dispatch. Retain scalar tails, 4-lane Wasm/NEON and x86 AVX2/FMA. Preserve all feature and target configurations. Do not expand another open issue or change DSP algorithms. Read current related issue bodies before touching their subject; discoveries that require architecture or product decisions become bounded follow-ups and final owner questions.

## Implementation and test-value decisions

Prefer deleting or consolidating repetition to adding abstractions that increase total complexity. Assess every existing test or a clearly named homogeneous family by its plausible unique defect; remove trivial, redundant or obsolete cases only after identifying the surviving behavioral gate. Keep independent numeric/oracle, fault, allocation, queue, boundary and target tests. Add/rewrite tests only for a concrete uncovered defect, and state which plausible defect no existing test catches. No prose/source-grep tests, new bit-digest pins or exact resource-byte pins. Copies needed for ownership, snapshots or atomic admission stay unless the same semantics are proved with less work. Data structure changes must preserve deterministic order and bounded realtime work. Inspect applicable hot loops and generated code before claiming additional SIMD; recursive/stateful dependencies alone do not justify changing arithmetic.

## Objective gates and evidence

- Read all production and test files in this package; record concise findings for each of the five requests, concrete changed/deferred locations, and load-bearing test families with retained coverage for deletions.
- Run focused locked package tests and affected feature configurations; use existing downstream/RT/differential gates proportional to the changed contract. Check formatting and package clippy with warnings denied. Relevant Wasm and AArch64 compile checks are required for changed product code; record limitations candidly.
- Changes to DSP arithmetic or hot state need existing independent numeric and scalar/SIMD gates plus one-time base/head evidence when needed; no permanent comparison against the old implementation. Existing research remains the algorithm authority; no new algorithm or listening claim is authorized.
- Benchmarks are optional and descriptive. Any timed measurement freezes its workload/validator, passes zero-workload preflight, and runs exactly one invocation with one warmup/two measured rounds. No timing optimization loop, performance percentage or unsupported sound-quality claim.
- Root conducts one adversarial verdict per coherent attempt, at most five total attempts. Every new/rewritten test gets its unique-defect sentence in that verdict. No-change audits require the same five-axis review, not manufactured edits.
- Stop after a coherent compiling, focused-green tranche; root commits exact owned paths before further edits. Keep edits within `tools/audit` and this numbered spec. Independent crates use separate worktrees. Root pushes promptly and updates this GitHub issue with evidence; close only after PASS and evidence upstream, verifying remote state. Merge through the required qualification check and remove clean completed worktrees.

## Sol brief approval and decision record

Approved 2026-10-01 by root Sol within the user's crate-by-crate housekeeping request. Attempt 1 is authorized with the frozen scope/gates above. Owner questions are collected for the final report; routine reversible cleanup proceeds autonomously. Scope is this package's housekeeping, not completion of pre-existing feature/bug issues.

## Attempt evidence

### Attempt 1 — complete package review and checkpoint

Worker A (GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh) read all 16 source files (13,220 baseline Rust lines), the manifest, both vectorization documents/allowlist, and the package's four fixture payloads plus manifest. Reviewed the external builtins corpus's manifest/provenance and existing read-only/mutation checkers. Related scopes #349/#559/#560, #377, #968 and the current R7/R9 ruling were read before the approved proposal. #377 continues to own structured disassembly/cross-artifact qualification; #968 owns fixture bank-width expansion. Neither scope is implemented here. Root approved the exact nine-path pass and checkpointed it at `d09048eb`, integrated/pushed as `4c0d4fde`; subsequent work is verification/evidence only.

**Size:** 61 added / 123 removed Rust lines (**−62**); including `VECTORIZATION.md`, 66 added / 128 removed (**−62**). Four identical parser functions became one; the unused private `Carveout::total` was removed. **No test functions added or retired: all 33 remain active.** No manifest, lock, allowlist, fixture, generator, schedule, DSP expression or public API changed.

### Five review axes and preservation

| Axis | Bounded result and retained reason |
| --- | --- |
| Repetition/LoC | `main::parse_blocks` replaces four byte-identical effect parsers, retaining defaults, missing/value/unknown errors, parse-before-frozen-count refusal and ignored trailing arguments. The distinct graph/realtime parsers and dispatch/reexec precedence remain. `complete_files` collects the existing generated map directly: its generator already emits the identical ten benchmark inputs. Removed compressor's unused preparation offsets/length assertion and the self-equal carveout assertion; actual bank offsets and all numeric observations remain. |
| Test value | Kept all independent numeric, malformed-input, ownership, allocation and format owners below. The two 24-input matrices reach distinct coverage holes and retain every original mutation. No obsolete output pin or new harness was introduced; existing fixture identities describe accepted on-disk formats. Removed assertions had no reachable defect: one compared a value with itself, the other counted an unused vector. |
| Copies | Disassembly lines append their whitespace tokens directly with the same single-space/newline normalization; failure JSON uses the existing string-array escaper with identical bytes/order/brackets. Three canonical record readers borrow the previous line, preserving canonicalization-before-order refusal. Untapped meter records move their existing canonical string; tapped records retain the same wrapper. Manifest serialization borrows ordered path/payload pairs instead of cloning the corpus. Six mutation UTF-8 views borrow original bytes before the same replacement/slicing operation. F5 reads its untouched original input/reversed input instead of cloning source buffers. Mutable render buffers, independent models and isolated corpus mutations still require ownership. |
| Micro SIMD | No new SIMD or arithmetic transformation is warranted in parser/fixture tooling. The current release artifact's W8 gain/sum/SVF probes use YMM `vmulps`/`vaddps` and direct vector loads/stores; SVF retains ordered compare/mask denormal flushing and persistent vector state. Existing certification rejects scalar FP arithmetic, FMA and calls in those bodies. These are 32-frame full banks, so this evidence does not establish tails or mobile codegen; unchanged production width/tail owners remain authoritative. No timing, base instruction-count or speed claim. |
| Data structures | Retained BTree maps/sets for deterministic canonical ordering, and distinct mutable corpus maps for mutation isolation. Removed duplicate map regeneration and per-line/intermediate formatting collections. The reference meter's short configured history is an independent, bounded non-render oracle; changing its queue or consolidating its equations would add complexity without a demonstrated housekeeping benefit. |

`VECTORIZATION.md` now distinguishes official mobile AArch64 support from this report's still-retired/unqualified NEON allowlist. Its AArch64 certification remains deliberately red; #377 owns that qualification. Intentional fused/unfused/f64 research models remain independent, while prose names the current unfused arm accurately. Remaining hand-written JSON lookup/model/manifest tooling belongs to the existing #560 TOOL4/TOOL5 and #377 scopes; no shared framework or owner decision is added.

## Root adversarial verdict: PASS — attempt 1

Root independently inspected all nine product diffs, the already-complete ordered fixture generator, manifest writer callers, F5 source/reversal ownership and canonical-line readers. The second generation of ten benchmark inputs was redundant; direct collection preserves their keys, bytes and order. Borrowed inputs outlive every reader and are not mutated during model evaluation. Whitespace/token and failure-array serialization preserve the exact normalization/escaping and parser refusal semantics. The four block parsers retain the same defaults and errors. No numerical expression, fixture, public API, dependency or allowlist changed.

All 33 original tests remain; no new test is claimed. For rewritten fixture test preparation, borrowing UTF-8 and manifest inputs preserves the existing format and corruption cases that detect malformed/missing tuple, parameter, identity and dependent hash defects; no duplicate test or weakened case replaces those owners. Existing vectorization mutation tests catch missing packed instructions, scalar/FMA/call contamination and ambiguous bodies through the same parser. Root read the actual debug/release, strict lint, fixture, mutation, installed-allocation, bounded model and target logs. The retired nonexistent math-policy command is recorded as a failed attempted command, not a gate. Native full-bank codegen and compile-only mobile/Wasm evidence are accurately limited; unchanged Wasm cfg warnings are disclosed.

The complete five-axis review earns the retained independent models and ordered data structures. Rust decreases by 62 lines, with no test functions added or removed and no measured speed claim. Evidence is sufficient for this bounded behavior-preserving housekeeping slice.
